findings.finding: The only functional assertion carries a binding named figma_document_state whose source_id is SRC-883e0f7bef1c8de5acdd5da5 (the frozen Figma snapshot) and whose reference_hash is the Figma packet contract hash, even though STATE-1 has origin DOCUMENT_ONLY and its sole authority is docs/spec.md (SRC-ec10b431bb2e0be0e2aee0cc). The assertion's own source block is correct, and the plan does disclose the situation, but the disclosure lives only in prose inside planContract.residual_risks, not in the uiAtomicityContract where the binding is consumed. A consumer that resolves provenance from figma_document_state.source_id alone would attribute a markdown-only behavioural requirement to the frozen design — which matters here because the design genuinely does show chip selection (Cuisses and Fessier rendered selected), a state the plan deliberately does not realize.
evidence: Observed figma-evidence/zones-reference.png: the 'Zones corporelles' modal renders Cuisses and Fessier as selected chips, confirming a real rendered selection concept distinct from the documentary Boolean; planContract residual_risks names 3302:4166, 4953:6620 and 4953:6625 as explicitly not realized.

findings.finding: The FUNCTIONAL_TEST proof is bound to target_test_impact_id IMP-8c5cc8ccf29e5c7c8e57ea7e (tests/ui.test.js) and justified as 'Execute the documentary toggle scenarios and preservation checks on the delivered implementation'. In the observed orchestration the scenario-level proof_results for toggle-off-on and toggle-on-off are not derived from that Node test at all: they are derived from the browser observer's own transition calls. The delivered test is executed and will abort the run if it throws, so the behaviour is still gated, but nothing in the recorded evidence ties the FUNCTIONAL_TEST proof status to the file the proof targets. A downstream auditor reconciling PROOF-d1579ccff96cf9d4524ffb52 against its target impact finds the scenario verdicts sourced from the same browser run that produces the VISUAL_COMPARE facts, which is the opposite of the independence the plan's two-proof split implies.

findings.finding: The only authored test obligation in the plan never requires the render() availability / string-return assertion that the plan elsewhere declares as a deliverable of tests/ui.test.js. TEST-4cc10621179bca6f85c26783.expected specifies exactly two blocks: the require.cache sentinel preservation block and the two-call toggle block. It then says the sentinel block must run "independently of render and toggle assertions", presupposing render assertions that it never defines. No other obligation defines them: the two visual test obligations are NONE_WITH_JUSTIFICATION and carry the VISUAL_COMPARE text instead. An implementer following the formal obligations would ship a test file with no render() assertion while the plan's own constraint claims that file delivers "render availability" checks.

findings.required_correction: Add the render() availability assertion to TEST-4cc10621179bca6f85c26783.expected (and mirror it in PROOF-d1579ccff96cf9d4524ffb52.expected), e.g. 'In a dedicated isolated child Node process, load Screen freshly, call render() with zero arguments and assert typeof the returned value is "string"', which is the text already drafted as QUALIFICATION_CONTRACT.visual_test_expected. If instead render() coverage is intended to rest solely on the external browser host, delete 'render availability' from the implementation_constraints sentence and the 'execute render() and assert a string return' clause from IMP-22a195df6bcc0cb6547c8491.impact_reason so the plan stops declaring an undefined test deliverable.

findings.finding: Both visual plan items assert 'The independent observer produces and verifies these facts; implementation cannot supply success flags.' The observed orchestration does not structurally guarantee this: the implementer's Screen.js bytes are injected as a classic <script> into the measured page, and the measurement expression is evaluated in that same JavaScript realm. Implementer code therefore has write access to the very primitives the measurement reads — Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect, Node textContent, document.querySelectorAll, innerHTML — before the observer evaluates them. The provenance attestation does not close this: loaded-document vs generated-host is compared in Node and is sound, but canonical_render and measured_mount are both computed inside the page (observer lines 124-125), so a prototype patch would corrupt both sides of that equality identically. The only barrier is the prose prohibition 'The implementation must not export or execute any adjustment to the independent observer or its measurements', i.e. a behavioural rule, not isolation. For a qualification whose stated purpose is falsification of a delivery, the strength claim exceeds the architecture.
evidence: planContract PROOF-d0b0542fbaf8c355b5268da6.expected and PROOF-94a25cce17d666c8a47d7fa7.expected: 'The independent observer produces and verifies these facts; implementation cannot supply success flags.'
planContract implementation_constraints: 'The implementation must not export or execute any adjustment to the independent observer or its measurements.' — a prohibition, not an isolation mechanism.

scripts/kodjo/lib/vnext-figma-browser-observer.js:119-128: the measurement Runtime.evaluate runs in the default execution context and reads document.querySelectorAll('[data-figma-id]'), frame.getBoundingClientRect(), title.textContent and subject[t.method]() — all patchable from the same realm.

scripts/kodjo/lib/vnext-figma-browser-observer.js:124-125: provenance.canonical_render and provenance.measured_mount are both produced in-page via template.innerHTML and mount.innerHTML, so attestProvenance's canonicalRender!==measuredMount check cannot detect a realm-level patch.
scripts/kodjo/lib/vnext-figma-browser-observer.js:81-89 host(): implementer bytes are interpolated into '<script>' and executed in the page realm, then window.subject=app.exports.
findings.required_correction: Either (a) make the claim structurally true by measuring from a separate JavaScript realm that shares the DOM — create the measurement context with Page.createIsolatedWorld and pass its executionContextId to the measurement Runtime.evaluate, keeping only the subject[t.method]() transition calls in the main world; or (b) if the current architecture is to be kept for this disposable run, downgrade the wording in PROOF-d0b0542fbaf8c355b5268da6, PROOF-94a25cce17d666c8a47d7fa7 and the matching TEST obligations from 'implementation cannot supply success flags' to the accurate 'the observer computes the comparisons; implementation bytes execute in the same page realm as the measurement, so realm-level tampering is prohibited by constraint rather than prevented', and add that limitation to residual_risks.
